rows.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about the males in a colony of honey bees ?
(i) They have 16 chromosomes per cell.
(ii) They produce sperms by meiosis.
(iii) They have a grandfather but no father.
(iv) All males in the colony are haploid except one.
rows.solution:
The males of a honey bee colony, the **drones**, develop from **unfertilised eggs** by parthenogenesis, so they are **haploid**.
- (i) A female (queen or worker) is diploid with 32 chromosomes, so a drone has half that number, **16 chromosomes** per cell. True.
- (ii) Because the drone is already haploid, it produces sperms by **mitosis**, not meiosis. False.
- (iii) A drone has no father, since it comes from an unfertilised egg, but its mother (the queen) came from a fertilised egg and so had a father. That male is the drone's **grandfather**. True.
- (iv) Every male in the colony is haploid; there is no exception. False.

So the true statements are (i) and (iii). So the answer is option (A) (i) and (iii) only.

rows.stem:
Match the correct Structures given in Column I with the Fruit in Column II in the chart given below :
| Column I (Structure) | Column II (Fruit) |
|---|---|
| P. Perisperm | i. Maize |
| Q. Thalamus | ii. Black pepper |
| R. Pericarp | iii. Strawberry |
| S. Endosperm | iv. Mango |
rows.solution:
- **Perisperm** is the residual, persistent nucellus seen in some seeds, such as **black pepper** and beet (P-ii).
- The **thalamus** contributes to the fruit in false fruits such as apple, **strawberry** and cashew (Q-iii).
- The **pericarp** is the wall of the fruit, developed from the wall of the ovary; in **mango** it is fleshy (R-iv).
- The **endosperm** persists in albuminous seeds such as wheat, **maize**, barley and castor (S-i).

So the answer is option (B) P-ii, Q-iii, R-iv, S-i.

rows.stem: Which of the following hormones are active during the ovulatory phase of menstrual cycle in a normal human female ?
rows.solution:
CBSE accepted 'FSH and LH', 'LH and Estrogen' and 'FSH and Estrogen' for this question.

The ovulatory phase falls in the middle of the menstrual cycle, about the 14th day. During the follicular phase that leads up to it, LH and FSH rise gradually, and both **LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle**. The rapid secretion of LH to its maximum level, the **LH surge**, induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle and so the release of the ovum (ovulation). Estrogen, secreted by the growing follicles, also peaks just before ovulation, which is why the combinations with estrogen were credited as well. Progesterone becomes important only after ovulation, when the corpus luteum forms in the luteal phase. So the answer is option (A) FSH and LH.

rows.stem: Which one of the following fixes the atmospheric nitrogen but is not an autotroph ?
rows.solution: Oscillatoria, Anabaena and Nostoc are **cyanobacteria**: they fix atmospheric nitrogen and are also **autotrophs**, making their own food by photosynthesis. **Rhizobium** is a symbiotic bacterium that lives in the root nodules of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen there, but it cannot photosynthesise; it is a **heterotroph** that obtains its food from the host plant. So the answer is option (B) Rhizobium.

rows.stem: Given below is a diagram of an ecological pyramid of numbers. Choose the correct food chain from the list of food chains given, that represents the given pyramid.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:four unlabelled rectangles stacked one on another as the four trophic levels of a pyramid of numbers, the producer level at the bottom; the relative widths of the four levels decide which food chain fits, so they are withheld here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
In a pyramid of numbers each bar stands for the number of individuals at one trophic level, with the producers at the base. The given pyramid has a broad base, a narrower second level, a still narrower third level and then a **broad top level**: the numbers fall from producers to herbivores to carnivores and then rise again at the top.

That fits a food chain that ends in a **parasite**: a great many grass plants support fewer rabbits, the rabbits support still fewer foxes, and each fox carries a large number of fleas. In the other chains the number of individuals keeps falling up to the top carnivore (tiger, cheetah, snake), which would give an ordinary upright pyramid. So the answer is option (C) Grass \(\rightarrow\) Rabbit \(\rightarrow\) Fox \(\rightarrow\) Flea.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : In a monohybrid cross between tall plants and dwarf plants, the \(\text{F}_2\) generation showed tall and dwarf plants in the ratio of 3 : 1.
Reason (R) : There is no blending of traits/characters in the \(\text{F}_2\) generation.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: When Mendel crossed true-breeding tall and dwarf pea plants, all the \(\text{F}_1\) plants were tall, and on self-pollination the \(\text{F}_2\) generation had tall and dwarf plants in the ratio **3 : 1**. The Assertion is true. The dwarf trait reappeared in the \(\text{F}_2\) generation exactly as it was in the parent, with no plants of intermediate height. This is because the two alleles do not mix or **blend** in the \(\text{F}_1\) hybrid; they stay separate and **segregate** into different gametes, so one quarter of the \(\text{F}_2\) plants receive two recessive alleles and are dwarf. So the absence of blending is what produces the 3 : 1 ratio. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Homo sapiens have evolved from chimpanzee-like ancestors.
Reason (R) : There is no difference between the two in the amino acid sequence of the protein Cytochrome-C.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Humans and chimpanzees share a recent common ancestor, so Homo sapiens arose from ape-like (chimpanzee-like) ancestors; the Assertion is accepted as true. Cytochrome c is a respiratory protein found in almost all organisms, and the more closely two species are related, the fewer the differences in its amino acid sequence. The cytochrome c of humans and chimpanzees has **no difference at all** in its amino acid sequence, so the Reason is also true. This identical sequence is **biochemical evidence** of the very close relationship between the two and so supports the Assertion; read that way, the Reason explains it. So both the Assertion and the Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion, which is option (A).

(Strictly, an identical protein sequence is evidence of a recent common ancestry rather than the cause of human evolution, and humans did not evolve from the chimpanzee itself. The marking scheme keys this pair as a correct explanation.)

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Breast-feeding is advised by the doctor as it is essential for the new borns.
Reason (R) : Colostrum secreted by the mother during initial days of lactation has abundant antibodies containing IgE and IgG.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: Breast-feeding is advised for a new-born because mother's milk gives complete nutrition and protects the baby from infection. The Assertion is true. The yellowish fluid **colostrum**, secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation, has abundant antibodies, but they are of the **IgA** type. These antibodies give the infant **passive immunity**. IgE is the antibody of allergic reactions and IgG is the main antibody of the blood, so the Reason is false. So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : The Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to the predators.
Reason (R) : The butterfly has a very rough skin which is not palatable.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution: The Monarch butterfly is highly **distasteful** to its predators, such as birds, so the Assertion is true. The reason is chemical, not physical: during its caterpillar stage it feeds on a **poisonous weed** and stores a special chemical from it in its body, which makes the butterfly unpalatable. A predator that has tried one avoids the others. It is not a rough skin that protects it, so the Reason is false. So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem: List and explain any two factors that lead to a decrease in the population density of an area.
rows.solution:
Population density changes with four basic processes: natality and immigration add individuals, while mortality and emigration remove them. Its change is given by \(N_{t+1} = N_t + [(B + I) - (D + E)]\). The two factors that **decrease** population density are:
- **Mortality (death rate)**: the number of deaths in the population during a given period. Deaths reduce the number of individuals present in the area.
- **Emigration**: the number of individuals of the population who leave the habitat and go elsewhere during the time period under consideration. Individuals that move out are no longer counted in the area's population.

When mortality and emigration together exceed natality and immigration, the population density falls.

rows.stem:
Explain the role of microorganisms in the following :
(a) Reducing the sugar content in grape juice
(b) Production of a fuel
rows.solution:
(a) **Reducing the sugar content in grape juice.** The yeast **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** (brewer's yeast) ferments the sugars in grape juice under anaerobic conditions, converting them into **ethanol (alcohol)** and carbon dioxide. So the sugar content falls as wine is produced; wine is made without distillation.

(b) **Production of a fuel.** Bacteria called **methanogens** (for example Methanobacterium) grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, such as the excreta (dung) of cattle, which is rich in it. In a biogas plant they break this material down to produce **biogas**, mainly methane with carbon dioxide and hydrogen, which is used as a fuel for cooking and lighting.

rows.stem:
The diagram given below shows the events occurring in an ovary during Oogenesis in a human female.
(a) Identify 'X'. Mention the time when the process occurs in a human female.
(b) Identify 'Y'. When and how is it formed ?
(c) Name the hormone produced by 'Z'.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a scanned sectional drawing of an ovary with a sequence of structures joined by arrows around it, and three pointer lines labelled 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'; which structure each label marks is what all three parts ask, so it is withheld here. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(a) 'X' is a **primary follicle**: a primary oocyte surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells. Oogenesis begins **during the fetal stage** (embryonic development): the oogonia formed in the fetal ovary enter meiosis I and stop at prophase I as primary oocytes, which become surrounded by granulosa cells to form primary follicles. No more oogonia are formed or added after birth.

(b) 'Y' is the **secondary oocyte** in the tertiary (Graafian) follicle. It is formed during the **follicular phase** of the menstrual cycle, between about the 6th and 13th day. The primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and **completes its first meiotic division**. This is an unequal division, giving a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny **first polar body**. The secondary oocyte keeps the bulk of the nutrient-rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte.

(c) 'Z' is the **corpus luteum**, formed from the remains of the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation. It secretes large amounts of **progesterone**, which is essential for maintaining the endometrium.

rows.stem:
(i) How many types of RNA polymerases are there in an eukaryote cell ? Mention which one of them transcribes hnRNA.
(ii) Write the changes that hnRNA undergoes before it leaves the nucleus as mRNA.
rows.solution:
(i) There are **three types of RNA polymerases** in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell:
- RNA polymerase I transcribes the rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S);
- RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the **heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA)**;
- RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.

So hnRNA is transcribed by **RNA polymerase II**.

(ii) Before it leaves the nucleus as mRNA, the hnRNA undergoes three changes:
- **Splicing**: the introns (non-coding sequences) are removed and the exons are joined in a definite order.
- **Capping**: an unusual nucleotide, methyl guanosine triphosphate, is added to the 5'-end of the hnRNA.
- **Tailing**: adenylate residues (200-300) are added at the 3'-end in a template-independent manner.

The fully processed hnRNA, now called mRNA, is transported out of the nucleus for translation.

(ii) Differentiate between the two newly synthesised DNA strands within the fork.

You are given a tall pea plant with green seeds. The genotype of this plant is unknown. You are allowed to do only 'selfing' of these plants to find out the genotype of the given plant.
Work out all possible crosses and show how you would determine the genotype of the given plant.
rows.solution:
In pea, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t), and yellow seed colour (Y) is dominant over green (y). A plant with **green seeds** must be homozygous recessive, **yy**, since green appears only without a yellow allele. A **tall** plant may be **TT or Tt**. So the given plant is either **TTyy** or **Ttyy**, and selfing tells the two apart.

**Case 1: the plant is TTyy.** Selfing TTyy \(\times\) TTyy: every gamete is Ty.

| Gametes | Ty |
|---|---|
| Ty | TTyy |

All the progeny are **tall with green seeds**; the plant breeds true. Conclusion: the given plant is homozygous dominant for height and homozygous recessive for seed colour, **TTyy**.

**Case 2: the plant is Ttyy.** Selfing Ttyy \(\times\) Ttyy: the gametes are Ty and ty.

| Gametes | Ty | ty |
|---|---|---|
| Ty | TTyy | Ttyy |
| ty | Ttyy | ttyy |

The genotypes are 1 TTyy : 2 Ttyy : 1 ttyy, so the progeny are **tall green : dwarf green in the ratio 3 : 1**. Conclusion: the given plant is heterozygous for height and homozygous recessive for seed colour, **Ttyy**.

So if all the offspring of selfing are tall, the plant is TTyy; if about one quarter are dwarf, it is Ttyy. All offspring have green seeds in either case.
